subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core global config surface with the PR's opt-in tier semantics, where omitted config preserves legacy behavior and only `full` includes hook-loaded extras?
rationale: This is a new public config/default surface that changes session context composition and overlaps existing bootstrap controls, so automation cannot decide the product contract on maintainer behalf.

options.title: Accept after contract cleanup
options.body: Proceed with this PR shape after fixing the no-override versus explicit-tier documentation and refreshing review against current main.

options.title: Revise the tier semantics
options.body: Ask for a different runtime contract, such as making omitted behavior map to a named tier or adding per-agent/session-specific tier controls before merge.

options.title: Decline the new knob
options.body: Close or pause the PR and steer users to existing `contextInjection`, bootstrap budget, and hook controls instead.

recommendation.title: Accept after contract cleanup
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR shape after fixing the no-override versus explicit-tier documentation and refreshing review against current main.
